chunks: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the statement of God, Mighty and Majestic:

'Yet when they felt Our punishment, behold, they (tried to) flee from it. Flee not, but return to the good things of this life which were given you, and to your homes in order that ye may be called to account.'

He said: When al-Qa'im makes his stand and sends (an army) to the Banu Umayya in Syria, they will flee to Rome. The Romans will say to them: 'We will not let you enter until you become Christians.' So they will hang crosses upon their necks and they will let them enter. When the companions of al-Qa'im descend upon them, (the Romans) will seek security and reconciliation. The companions of al-Qa'im will say: 'We will not do that until you hand over to us those who came to you from among us.' So they will hand them over.
That is His statement: 'Flee not, but return to the good things of this life which were given you, and to your homes in order that ye may be called to account.'

He said: He (al-Qa'im) will question them about the treasures, though he knows more than they do about them. He said: They will say: 'O woe unto us! Verily, we were wrongdoers.' They will not cease that invocation of theirs until We make them reaped and extinguished by the sword.

key_terms.الرُّومُ: Al-Rum — Byzantines/Romans, historical Christian empire to the north/west of Syria
key_terms.الصُّلْبَانُ: Al-Sulban — crosses, worn as the Umayyads accept Christianity to gain Byzantine protection
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: Al-Qa'im — 'The Rising One', a title for the awaited Imam Mahdi (the twelfth Imam) who will rise to establish justice
key_terms.الْكُنُوزُ: Al-Kunuz — treasures, the hidden/unlawful wealth that the Qa'im will demand accounting for
key_terms.بَنُو أُمَيَّةَ: Banu Umayya — the Umayyad dynasty, regarded in Shia tradition as usurpers and oppressors of the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about al-Qa'im and the Banu Umayya in the end times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides an eschatological interpretation of Quran 21:12-13, applying these verses about the destruction of ancient oppressive communities to the end-times events surrounding the rise of al-Qa'im (Imam Mahdi). The narrative describes the Umayyads fleeing from Syria to the Byzantines upon the Qa'im's military advance, their apostasy in hanging crosses to gain entry, and their ultimate destruction. The vivid Quranic imagery of communities 'fleeing' divine punishment is thus understood to prophesy the specific fate of the Umayyad dynasty under the Qa'im's just rule.
